limitations: One original wallet/network, two durable outboxes, chain nonces zero through two, one unrelated pending transaction and one configured-wallet rotation. Signed bytes and transaction identity remain immutable; activity from the replacement wallet is outside this model.
Signing and persistence commit atomically under the wallet lock. One matching successful chain receipt is trusted as nonce consumption; arbitrary reorgs, RPC dishonesty and cryptography are excluded.

Account deletion preserves unconfirmed signed authority. Terminal recovery observes the original receipt without another send. The model does not establish TypeScript/SQL refinement, safe retry of reverted sweeps, or liveness.

A matching original receipt remains recoverable after configuration rotation. Any new send still requires current-wallet authorization; disabled networks and unbounded external configuration changes are not modeled.
Two PostgreSQL transactions, one payment and one sweep outbox. Receipt publication and deletion take the payment lock before its child outbox lock.

Deletion retains unconfirmed signed authority. Transaction completion or rollback releases both row locks. A matching receipt is already available; provider receipt validity is covered by the nonce model.
The model checks this finite lock order and includes the reversed-order deadlock witness. It does not establish fairness, database implementation refinement or freedom from unrelated lock cycles.
Three callers and physical reads; generation and revision range over 0..2. Credential startup and queued credential writes have settled before modeled read allocation.
A revision change prevents joining an older read. Existing callers may still receive an older revision; only generation fences returned data.

The model checks shared-read identity, conditional finalizer cleanup and account-generation rejection. Native gateway and provider response classification are exercised by the conformance hook, not proved by this model.
Provider state can change within one network round trip. No network fairness, permission freshness beyond that window, JavaScript refinement or external-system liveness is proved.

A shared 20-second AbortSignal deadline covers fetch and body parsing. Its callback must be scheduled and the transport must honor abort; timeout settles as unavailable, never as authorization success. Timer fairness and wall-clock delivery are not proved.

Two namespaces and one old session plus one already-admitted preparation. The real binding switch retains the old namespace but does not route old session IDs to it.

The target namespace must first exist through operator host-only provisioning; missing target blocks activation. The release gate checks live admission freeze, exact source/namespace identity and decision-time attestation expiry twice. Drain is human-trusted evidence, not measured by the gate. The proved step assumes that claim is true, includes all in-flight preparations, and admission remains quiesced until the switch; excluded false-claim and thaw witnesses violate safety.

Provider closure and terminal accounting are separate abstract acknowledgements. Namespace retention and receipt ordering do not prove eventual retirement, Cloudflare propagation, rollout readiness, live latency or TypeScript refinement. Real Workerd tests demonstrate the old-session routing boundary; metadata and shell tests exercise the release gate.
One retained Cloud encoder slot, two encoding kinds, three asynchronous loads and two callers.
Each caller retains its own load promise. Replacing the cached encoding does not replace an existing caller's result; failure clears only the matching cache entry.

Timer cancellation and callbacks follow a single JavaScript event loop. Rank-module contents, exact BPE output and idle-release behavior are checked by the real implementation conformance hook. The hook also checks the real API-server import graph.

The OpenAI per-encoding persistent cache is regression-tested by the hook but is not represented by the one-slot model. No GC reclamation deadline, network/scheduler fairness or TypeScript refinement is proved.
